slides.heading: Merge Sort
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Sorting
slides.narration: Let's solve Merge Sort, a very hard sorting problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Stable divide-and-conquer sort using one auxiliary buffer.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Stable divide-and-conquer sort using one auxiliary buffer.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Split in half, sort each half, then merge the sorted halves.
slides.narration: Split in half, sort each half, then merge the sorted halves.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Merge sort → O(n log n), stable
slides.narration: Merge sort guarantees n log n and is stable, at the cost of an auxiliary array.

slides.heading: Approach
slides.narration: Step by step. First, recurse on halves. Second, merge using a buffer. Third, copy back.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Split in half recursively
slides.narration: Split the array in half repeatedly until pieces have one element.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Sort both halves
slides.narration: After recursion, both halves are sorted.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Merge with two pointers
slides.narration: Merge by repeatedly taking the smaller front element.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Sort recurses on both halves, copies the range to aux, and merges back taking the smaller of the two fronts.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n log n. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Allocate the auxiliary array once, not per call.
